ticket.title: Patient search results unmount and remount on every keystroke, causing multi-second UI stalls and heap growth
ticket.text:
Patient search results unmount and remount on every keystroke, causing multi-second UI stalls and heap growth

## Symptom

In the patient search (both the compact dropdown and the advanced search page), every keystroke that changes the query causes the entire rendered banner list to unmount and remount. With ~50 accumulated patient banners (e.g. five auto-paginated pages of ten), this:

- triggers ~150 simultaneous backend requests (per-banner `/obs` photo lookup, `/visit`, `/person`) within a few ms
- blocks the JS main thread long enough that the next keystroke event sits in the event queue for multiple seconds before dispatching
- accumulates promise-reaction / SWR-subscriber state in the heap that does not appear to be released

In one captured session, a single keypress took 3.7 s to register as a network request, and three Firefox heap snapshots taken seconds apart showed `mCallback` edges growing 75k → 153k → 458k.

## Reproduce

1. Open the patient search workspace (compact dropdown is enough).
2. Type a query that returns many results, e.g. `10`.
3. Scroll the results so the IntersectionObserver auto-paginates a few times (accumulate ~50 banners).
4. Type one more character and watch DevTools Network + Performance:

   - 100+ simultaneous `/obs?patient=…&concept=…` and `/visit?patient=…` requests fire.

   - The new `/patient?q=…` request is delayed by 1–5 s after the keypress.

1. Repeat several times and take Memory snapshots; retained heap grows monotonically.

## Root cause

`useInfinitePatientSearch` (`@openmrs/esm-patient-search-app/src/patient-search.resource.tsx:83`) calls `useSWRInfinite` without `keepPreviousData`. When `searchQuery` changes:

- `getUrl` returns URLs for the new query → SWR sees a new key sequence.
- `data` resets to `undefined`, `isLoading` becomes `true`.

Both view components gate on `isLoading` and return a skeleton/loader, throwing away the entire results subtree:

- `compact-patient-search/patient-search.component.tsx:52` → `<Loader />`
- `patient-search-page/patient-search-lg.component.tsx:41` → `<LoadingState />`

Every accumulated `<PatientBanner key={patient.uuid}>` unmounts, then remounts when the response arrives. Per remounted banner the fan-out is:

- `PatientPhoto` → `usePatientPhoto` → `/obs?patient=…&concept=<photoConceptUuid>&v=full`
- `useVisit(patientUuid)` called directly in `PatientBanner` (`patient-banner.component.tsx:41`)
- `VisitTag` extension from `esm-patient-banner-app` → another `useVisit(patientUuid)`
- start-visit-button slot → potentially another `useVisit`
- `/person/<uuid>` lookups for contact-details / deceased state

Compounding factor: `useSWRInfinite`'s `size` is not reset on key change. After auto-paginating to `size=5`, every subsequent keystroke immediately fires five pages of the new query in parallel. Tracked separately in O3-5715.

## Proposed fix

Two changes, applied together:

### 1. Keep previous data during query-change fetches

Add `keepPreviousData: true` to the `useSWRInfinite` call in `useInfinitePatientSearch`:

```typescript
const { data, isLoading, isValidating, setSize, error, size } = useSWRInfinite(
  shouldFetch ? getUrl : null,
  openmrsFetch,
  { keepPreviousData: true },
);
```

This keeps the banner list mounted across query changes. With stable `key={patient.uuid}`, React reuses banners for patients still in the new results, so no remount → no fan-out → no main-thread stall. `isLoading` then stays false on subsequent searches (only true on the very first load), and the loader gates in the view components don't tear down the subtree. `isValidating` can drive a non-disruptive loading hint if one is desired.

### 2. Harden the loader gates

Change both view components' loader gates so they only swap in the full skeleton when there is genuinely nothing to show:

- `compact-patient-search/patient-search.component.tsx:52` — `if (isLoading)` → `if (isLoading && !searchResults?.length)`
- `patient-search-page/patient-search-lg.component.tsx:41` — `if (isLoading)` → `if (isLoading && !results?.length)`

The `keepPreviousData` change above already keeps `isLoading` false during query-change fetches, but tightening the gate makes the intent explicit ("only show the full skeleton when we have nothing to show") and removes any reliance on SWR's `isLoading` semantics holding across versions.

Leave the existing next-page indicator (the small `<Loading withOverlay={false} small />` at `patient-search.component.tsx:94-96`) untouched — it fires off `hasMore` / `isValidating`, not `isLoading`, and is the right indicator for auto-pagination.

## Evidence

- HAR file from 2026-05-28T10:19:28 – 10:23:22 showing 24 patient searches with response-end → first-side-effect-request gaps ranging 20 ms (idle UI) to 5.7 s (stalled UI), with the burst always firing the moment the thread frees.
- Three Firefox heap snapshots taken seconds apart showing 141 MB → 161 MB → 181 MB retained, with `mCallback`, `mCreationStack`, `mIncumbentJSGlobal` edge counts roughly doubling per snapshot.

understanding.intent: Keep existing patient search results mounted while new search queries are loading so the UI does not unmount, stall, or display a full skeleton loader when results already exist.

criteria.text: When typing into patient search while previous results are displayed, the existing search result banners remain visible and mounted until new results arrive rather than being replaced by a full skeleton loader.
criteria.quote: This keeps the banner list mounted across query changes. With stable key={patient.uuid}, React reuses banners for patients still in the new results, so no remount → no fan-out → no main-thread stall.

criteria.text: In both compact patient search and the advanced search page, the full loader skeleton is only displayed when loading and there are no search results to show.
criteria.quote: Change both view components' loader gates so they only swap in the full skeleton when there is genuinely nothing to show

criteria.text: The small next-page loading indicator for auto-pagination continues to function and remain visible when fetching additional pages.
